reply:
`typeof null` returns `'object'` in all JavaScript engines, including modern ones. This was not fixed in ES6 or any later version.

TC39 considered fixing it but decided against it. Changing it would break existing code that guards against objects with `typeof v === 'object'`. The quirk remains.

What would change my mind: A link to ECMAScript spec documentation showing `typeof null` defined as returning `'null'`, or a demo in a current Node/browser showing it.
